<description>
## Summary
Follow-up to https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35384#issuecomment-4750866299

- Renamed `common::WriteSettings` to `common::WriteJson`.
- `WriteJson` writes to `path + ".tmp"` and `RenameOver()`s into place, so a failed or interrupted write cannot leave a truncated destination. Both `settings.json` and `banlist.json` use this helper.
- Added a unit test for the write/read roundtrip, that the `.tmp` is gone after success, that rename failure is detected, and that a second failed write overwrites the same `.tmp` rather than creating another.
</description>

A small example of this is error messages. Because `WriteSettings` is now shared by two kinds of files, this PR changes its errors from "settings file" to "JSON file", which is less clear for `settings.json`. `ReadSettings` has the opposite problem: its [parse error](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/9f2077dc09c98e093e15c605ef292669ef409f1d/src/common/settings.cpp#L90-L91) talks about a settings file and says removing it "will reset settings to default values", which is wrong for `banlist.json` (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35763#discussion_r4563647011). This PR doesn't change `ReadSettings`, so it doesn't make that harder to fix, but in both cases the caller is what knows which file it is (`CBanDB::Read` already [adds](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/9f2077dc09c98e093e15c605ef292669ef409f1d/src/addrdb.cpp#L168-L171) "Cannot load banlist" to the message) and what happens if it is removed. I think messages are easier to get right if low-level functions just read and write JSON and callers add the context as I originally suggested https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35384#issuecomment-4750866299. Still not a blocker for me.
[2026-11-13] rc:4563647011 inline on src/common/settings.cpp by ryanofsky (member) (edited 2026-11-13):
In commit "refactor: move .tmp handling into common::WriteSettings" (9f2077dc09c98e093e15c605ef292669ef409f1d)

Note: not for this PR, but a possible follow-up. The PR makes a truncated `banlist.json` less likely, but the way the truncated file is handled still seems unsafe to me. A truncated `settings.json` fails to parse and is [reported as an error](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/9f2077dc09c98e093e15c605ef292669ef409f1d/src/common/init.cpp#L100-L104) at startup. A truncated `banlist.json` fails to parse the same way, but `CBanDB::Read` [only logs a warning](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/9f2077dc09c98e093e15c605ef292669ef409f1d/src/addrdb.cpp#L168-L173), and [`BanMan::LoadBanlist`](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/9f2077dc09c98e093e15c605ef292669ef409f1d/src/banman.cpp#L41-L45) resets to an empty banlist, which the `BanMan` constructor [immediately writes](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/9f2077dc09c98e093e15c605ef292669ef409f1d/src/banman.cpp#L20-L21) over the corrupt file. So the bans are lost, and the file that would show what happened is gone.
[2026-11-13] rc:4563756700 inline on src/addrdb.cpp by ryanofsky (member) (edited 2026-11-13):
In commit "util: write banlist.json through a temporary file" (4a0f4916f60d31ec38afea3c141e7c8f53ffa46b)

The second commit [reverts the changes](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35763/changes/9f2077dc09c98e093e15c605ef292669ef409f1d#diff-a86c3e4f3b8f46384cbbbc5104be50f5637a030ffeb52a83bd207abeb0e72fab) this commit makes to `CBanDB::Write`, so across the PR `addrdb.cpp` doesn't change at all. That would seem more reasonable if the change being reverted were minimal, but this commit also restructures the function to return early on failure instead of on success, which the fix doesn't need.

Ideally I'd like to see (1) this commit reduced to a minimal bugfix without the restructuring, something like:

```diff
 bool CBanDB::Write(const banmap_t& banSet)
 {
+    const fs::path banlist_tmp{m_banlist_json + ".tmp"};
     std::vector<std::string> errors;
-    if (common::WriteSettings(m_banlist_json, {{JSON_KEY, BanMapToJson(banSet)}}, errors)) {
-        return true;
+    if (common::WriteSettings(banlist_tmp, {{JSON_KEY, BanMapToJson(banSet)}}, errors)) {
+        if (RenameOver(banlist_tmp, m_banlist_json)) return true;
+        errors.emplace_back(strprintf("Failed renaming JSON file %s to %s", fs::PathToString(banlist_tmp), fs::PathToString(m_banlist_json)));
     }
```

and (2) the second commit dropped, which would also match the design I'd prefer (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35763#discussion_r4563641406). But I'm also happy to see this merged as-is, or in any other form that fixes the bug.
[2026-11-13] r:5890638406 review APPROVED by ryanofsky (member) (edited 2026-11-13):
Code review ACK 9f2077dc09c98e093e15c605ef292669ef409f1d. `banlist.json` is now written through a temporary file and `RenameOver()`, like `settings.json`, so a crash or full disk during the write can no longer leave it truncated.

Thanks for the updates and the clear commit messages. Remaining comments are minor and can be ignored: the PR title and description still describe the earlier `WriteJson` version (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35763#discussion_r4563027281), the commits could be simpler, with a minimal fix in the first commit and no second commit (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35763#discussion_r4563653108), and there is a possible follow-up about how a corrupt `banlist.json` is handled (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35763#discussion_r4563647011).
